prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- A former Utah policeman is a suspect in at least three of Monday's four rush-hour shootings near Dallas, Texas, including one of two fatal attacks, police said Tuesday. CNN affiliate KSL in Salt Lake City, Utah, provided this file photo of the Dallas suspect, Brian Smith. The suspect, Brian Smith, tried to commit suicide after the Monday-evening shootings and was in a hospital in serious condition, Dallas police detective Lt. Craig Miller said. Police used ballistic tests to link Smith, a Utah state police officer for 12 years, to the shootings in which one driver was killed, one was injured by shattered glass and one escaped uninjured, Dallas police detective Lt. Craig Miller said. Miller said it is unclear if Smith was involved in the other fatal shooting, which was the first attack of the evening. Four motorists were attacked along a three-mile stretch near and on the LBJ Freeway, about 10 miles northeast of downtown Dallas, on Monday evening, police said. The first attack, which happened in Garland, Texas, about 5:41 p.m., killed Jorge Lopez. Garland police said Lopez, 20, was sitting in his Nissan at a traffic light when a man in a pickup pulled alongside him and fired shots into his car, killing him.   A few minutes after the Garland shooting and two miles away on LBJ Freeway, a gunman fired at two tractor-trailers. While one driver escaped injuries, William Scott Miller, 42, of Frankfort, Kentucky, was shot to death behind the wheel of a United Van Lines truck, police said. "He was going to be traveling home," Craig Miller said. "He was about to park his rig. He was going to get on a plane to fly to be with his wife and children for the Christmas season and then come back to this location." Miller called the truck driver a hero, saying he was able to control his rig before he died -- preventing other motorists from being hurt. The fourth attack came a mile west on LBJ Freeway when gunfire shattered the windshield of another tractor-trailer. The bullets missed the driver, but flying glass caused minor cuts, police said. Miller said video from the Garland shooting is available, and specialists were trying to enhance it to bring out details. Businesses along the other routes also may have video that will help police, he said. A friend of Lopez's said he was "a straight-up good guy, never had problems with anybody, never started anything with anybody." "So that's why this seems so out of the blue," Lopez's friend said.

outputs.L1:
(CNN) — A former Utah police officer is suspected in at least three of Monday’s four rush-hour shootings near Dallas, Texas, including one of two fatal attacks, police said Tuesday.

CNN affiliate KSL in Salt Lake City, Utah, provided a file photo of the suspect, Brian Smith.

Smith attempted suicide after the Monday evening shootings and was hospitalized in serious condition, Dallas police Detective Lt. Craig Miller said.

Ballistic tests linked Smith, who served as a Utah state police officer for 12 years, to three shootings in which one driver was killed, another suffered injuries from shattered glass, and a third escaped unharmed, Miller said. It remains unclear whether Smith was involved in the evening’s first attack, which was also fatal.

Four motorists were attacked Monday evening along a three-mile stretch near and on the LBJ Freeway, about 10 miles northeast of downtown Dallas, police said.

The first attack occurred in Garland, Texas, at about 5:41 p.m. and killed Jorge Lopez. Garland police said Lopez, 20, was sitting in his Nissan at a traffic light when a man in a pickup truck pulled alongside him and fired into his car, killing him.

A few minutes later, about two miles away on the LBJ Freeway, a gunman fired at two tractor-trailers. One driver escaped injury, but William Scott Miller, 42, of Frankfort, Kentucky, was shot and killed behind the wheel of a United Van Lines truck, police said.

“He was going to be traveling home,” Craig Miller said. “He was about to park his rig. He was going to get on a plane to fly to be with his wife and children for the Christmas season and then come back to this location.”

Miller called the truck driver a hero, saying he managed to maintain control of his rig before he died, preventing other motorists from being injured.

The fourth attack occurred a mile farther west on the LBJ Freeway, where gunfire shattered the windshield of another tractor-trailer. The bullets missed the driver, but flying glass caused minor cuts, police said.

Miller said video footage of the Garland shooting is available and that specialists were working to enhance it to reveal additional details. Businesses along the other routes may also have footage that could assist investigators, he said.

A friend described Lopez as “a straight-up good guy” who “never had problems with anybody” and “never started anything with anybody.”

“So that’s why this seems so out of the blue,” the friend said.

(CNN) — Dallas-area authorities said Tuesday that Brian Smith, a former Utah law enforcement officer, is suspected in at least three of the four shootings that targeted motorists during Monday evening’s rush hour. One of the three attacks linked to him was fatal.

CNN affiliate KSL in Salt Lake City, Utah, supplied a file photograph of Smith.

Dallas police Detective Lt. Craig Miller said Smith attempted suicide after the shootings and was hospitalized in serious condition. Ballistics evidence connected Smith, who served as a Utah state police officer for 12 years, to three incidents in which one driver died, another suffered minor cuts from broken glass, and a third was not hurt.

Investigators have not determined whether Smith was connected to the evening’s first shooting, which also resulted in a death, Miller said.

Police said four drivers were attacked Monday night along or near a three-mile section of the LBJ Freeway, roughly 10 miles northeast of downtown Dallas.

The first shooting occurred at approximately 5:41 p.m. in Garland, Texas. According to Garland police, 20-year-old Jorge Lopez was stopped at a traffic signal in his Nissan when a man driving a pickup truck pulled up next to him and fired into the vehicle, killing him.

Minutes later, about two miles away on the LBJ Freeway, someone shot at two tractor-trailers. One trucker was unharmed, but William Scott Miller, 42, of Frankfort, Kentucky, was fatally shot while driving a United Van Lines truck, police said.

Craig Miller said the truck driver had been preparing to park his vehicle and travel home by plane to spend Christmas with his wife and children before returning to the area. He described William Scott Miller as a hero because, despite being mortally wounded, he kept the truck under control and prevented other motorists from being injured.

The fourth shooting took place another mile west on the LBJ Freeway. Bullets shattered the windshield of a different tractor-trailer but did not strike its driver, who sustained minor cuts from flying glass, authorities said.

Craig Miller said investigators had obtained video of the Garland attack and that specialists were working to enhance the footage so additional details could be seen. He added that businesses located along the routes of the other shootings might also have useful recordings.

One of Lopez’s friends described him as an unquestionably good person who did not cause trouble or have conflicts with others, saying that his death therefore appeared completely unexpected.

# Two Killed in Series of Rush-Hour Shootings Near Dallas; Former Trooper Linked to Three Attacks

**DALLAS —** Four motorists were shot at in a series of attacks near Dallas during Monday evening’s rush hour, leaving two people dead and prompting a wide-ranging investigation into what authorities believe were connected shootings.

Investigators have linked former Utah state trooper Brian Smith to three of the attacks through ballistic evidence, according to information released in the case. Police are continuing to examine whether he was involved in the fourth incident.

Smith was hospitalized after an apparent suicide attempt. His condition and the circumstances surrounding the attempt were not immediately available. Authorities have not announced any charges.

The shootings occurred as commuters traveled through the Dallas area Monday evening. Two motorists were fatally wounded, while shots were also fired at two other drivers. Officials have not released the victims’ names or provided further details about injuries sustained in the nonfatal attacks.

Ballistics testing connected firearms evidence from three of the shooting scenes to Smith, giving investigators a key link between incidents that initially may have appeared separate. Authorities have not disclosed what type of weapon was used, how Smith was identified as a suspect or whether a firearm was recovered.

Police are reviewing surveillance video as they work to reconstruct the sequence of events. Investigators are expected to examine footage from traffic cameras, nearby businesses and other locations along the motorists’ routes. The review could help establish the suspect’s movements, identify vehicles connected to the attacks and clarify whether the victims were selected at random.

No possible motive has been made public, and authorities have not said whether Smith knew any of the motorists. Investigators also have not explained why ballistic evidence has linked him to only three of the four attacks.

Smith previously served as a state trooper in Utah. Details about his law-enforcement career, including when and why he left the agency, were not immediately available.

The investigation remains active as police seek additional evidence and determine whether anyone else was involved. Authorities are also working to establish a complete timeline of the shootings and the events leading to Smith’s hospitalization.

**Police seek video in deadly Garland, LBJ Freeway shootings**

**DALLAS, Texas (CNN)** — Police investigating a series of shootings in Garland and along LBJ Freeway are searching for surveillance footage that could identify the gunman or the vehicle used in the attacks.

Jorge Lopez was killed in the Garland shooting, authorities said. Truck driver William Scott Miller was fatally shot in a separate attack while driving on LBJ Freeway.

Two other drivers were also fired upon but survived. Investigators were interviewing the surviving motorists in hopes that they could provide a description of the shooter, a vehicle or other details linking the attacks.

Garland Detective Lt. Craig Miller said investigators were examining whether the shootings were connected and were working with other law-enforcement agencies. He said the apparently random nature of the gunfire made the case particularly troubling, while cautioning that detectives had not established a motive.

Police were seeking recordings from traffic cameras, nearby businesses and other surveillance systems along the routes where the shootings occurred. Investigators hoped video evidence would help establish a timeline and show vehicles that were in the area during the attacks.

Authorities asked anyone who witnessed suspicious activity or had relevant video to contact police.

A former police officer emerged as the principal suspect in three of the attacks. Detectives focused on his movements, weapons and possible motives while comparing ballistic and witness evidence from the scenes. The fourth shooting remained under separate investigation, with authorities cautioning against assuming it was related merely because it occurred nearby.

The most remarkable victim was a truck driver who was mortally wounded while operating his rig. Despite his injury, he retained control long enough to guide the truck to a safe stop, preventing the driverless vehicle from plowing into other traffic. He died from the gunshot wound, but investigators and witnesses credited his final actions with averting an even greater tragedy.
